summary: Re-read after T1 replaced its mechanism, then amended again when the task stage raised a signal: the plan asserted a 93-red suite, and a clean sequential run is 942 passed, 0 failed. The 93 was a non-hermetic board probe plus sharding under CPU contention. The baseline comparator T1 carried for that premise is CUT, the task order is now justified by dependency alone, and the Verify Plan states the suite is green. The four coherence findings from the read remain resolved as recorded.
gaps: Acceptance criterion 8, the generated-command grammar check, appeared in the plan but no task claimed the next-step renderer and parser surface.
The manifest named only the gate artifact and the accepted decisions, so a pass could omit a record it actually relied on, validate, and stay fresh after that record changed.
contradictions: The plan made every gate manifest-fresh after stage start while also giving T4 a non-manifest selective snapshot, which would have staled every post-stage task pass on any newly accepted decision and broken 0066's binding.
The task order declared T1 and T2 interchangeable while T1 carries the test-baseline comparator that every later stage needs to close against a 93-red suite.
resolutions: Post-stage task freshness is an exception to the manifest, stated as such: 0066 stands and binds that gate to its objective, criteria, plan contracts, user-facing flag and plan. Superseding 0066 was rejected because 0066 is the promise this story restores.
The recorder derives the manifest from the final pass payload, resolves every cited record to a repo-relative path, and refuses the pass when a cited input cannot be resolved.
T3 owns acceptance criterion 8, since it is the task that changes the next-step text and the board.
The order is now T1, T2, T3, T4, with each later task recording the comparator among its own verify commands.
The 93-red premise is removed from Scope, Acceptance Criteria, Risks and the Verify Plan; T1 loses the baseline comparator and its committed baseline, and the probe bug is fixed separately.
